name: 18844-bigbatch1k-8bfp8-1gpu
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1), sm90.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine.
architecture: LlamaForCausalLM: 32 layers, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, hidden 4096, intermediate 14336, max_position_embeddings 131072, torch_dtype bfloat16; static per-tensor FP8 (compressed-tensors) weights and activations, 8.46 GiB in two shards; KV 128 KiB per token.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=256, bounded at 2560 requests (ten waves of 256) with a 1800 s safety cap, warmup the first 10% by completion -- exactly the first wave. Saturating at this shape, deliberately.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets. Prompt exactly 1000 tokens and output exactly 100 (min = max on both); the backend forces ignore_eos=True when max_tokens is set, so every request has the same shape. The chat template plus add_special_tokens puts ~1011 tokens on the wire per prompt, not 1000.
purpose: A high-volume document summarizer serving 256 concurrent users thousand-token passages with brief summaries on one GPU.
launch:
# A stock single-GPU serve of an FP8 8B chat checkpoint, driven at a saturating batch.
# Nothing here is tuned; everything not listed is left at the engine's own default.

model: RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16

# NOT a redundant default. `vllm serve` gets its scheduler budget from `_set_default_args_v1`,
# which keys off the usage context; an engine built in-process reports one that is absent from
# that table, so this key alone falls through to DEFAULT_MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS = 2048.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

# Stated for symmetry, though it would survive on its own: `_set_default_args_v1` sets 1024
# unconditionally on a >=70 GiB device, so the SchedulerConfig 128 fallback is unreachable here.
# Named so the declared concurrency does not quietly depend on that staying true.
max-num-seqs: 1024
